final.memo:
Alphabet remains a wonderful business. In our view, the core search franchise continues to exhibit a durable moat, evidenced by an 18% consolidated revenue growth rate in the fourth quarter of 2025 [D03]. Perhaps more importantly, the Cloud segment has transitioned from a promising project to a significant contributor, with operating income jumping to $5.3 billion in the quarter alone [D03].

We are mindful of the significant capital expenditure plan of $175-$185 billion for 2026 [D01]. While this reflects an intense infrastructure commitment, our long-term focus remains on the durable earning power of the enterprise rather than short-term fluctuations in capital allocation [D01, D05]. A business earning such high returns on capital, even with rising physical asset requirements, is not something we sell simply because the market price has reached a certain level [D03, D04].

We do not look to flip stocks; we look to hold businesses. Given the 21% federal tax rate on realized gains, selling a productive, cash-generating franchise like Alphabet is a high hurdle that has not been cleared [D04]. We will continue to monitor management's ability to navigate the evolving antitrust and competitive landscape, but for now, we are comfortable holding our position [D05].
